_metadata.note: Paraphrased facts and direct RadLab observations. Review wording before player release.

facts.text: An OSDR study reports that wild-type mice lost significant muscle and bone mass during 33 days in microgravity.
facts.text_kids: In one spaceflight study, mice lost muscle and bone during 33 days in microgravity.
facts.source_name: NASA Open Science Data Repository dataset record

facts.text: The same OSDR study reports that muscle weights of Mstn -/- mice were largely maintained during spaceflight.
facts.text_kids: In the same study, mice with a special gene change kept more of their muscle during spaceflight.
facts.source_name: NASA Open Science Data Repository dataset record

facts.text: The OSDR study reports that blocking MSTN/activin A signaling increased muscle and bone mass in both ground and flight mice.
facts.text_kids: Scientists tested a treatment that helped increase muscle and bone in both Earth and space groups of mice.
facts.source_name: NASA Open Science Data Repository dataset record

facts.text: A NASA page describing OSDR-based research reports spaceflight-related gene-expression changes linked to frailty and muscle loss.
facts.text_kids: Spaceflight can change body signals linked to weaker muscles, so scientists study ways to protect astronauts.
facts.source_name: NASA, Aging and Fragility Biomarkers are Altered by Spaceflight

facts.text: The saved RadLab ISS sample records DosTel1 at 9.815504 micrograys per hour absorbed dose rate on 2022-04-01 at 23:00:00.
facts.text_kids: A RadLab detector on the space station recorded a radiation dose-rate reading during the sample time.

facts.text: The saved RadLab ISS sample records DosTel2 at 10.2160856666667 micrograys per hour absorbed dose rate on 2022-04-01 at 23:00:00.
facts.text_kids: A second RadLab detector recorded a nearby radiation dose-rate reading at the same sample time.
